results.title: The Louvre: a complete visitor's guide
results.content: The Louvre is the world's most visited museum, home to some 35,000 works on display across eight curatorial departments, from Egyptian antiquities to Italian Renaissance painting. Built as a fortress in the late twelfth century under Philip II, it became a royal palace and then, after the Revolution, a public museum in 1793. The glass pyramid designed by I. M. Pei opened in 1989 and is now the main entrance. Visitors are advised to plan a route in advance: the Denon wing holds the Mona Lisa, the Sully wing the medieval moats, and the Richelieu wing the Napoleon III apartments. Tickets are timed, and booking online is strongly recommended, particularly at weekends and during school holidays. On Sundays the museum opens at {open}.
